items.description:
The official source code of OpenSees is available on Github! See the repository!
The OpenSeesPy package is available on PyPi. Install the package!
items.title: Source Code

items.description: OpenSees plugins for existing welcomed text editors.

items.title: OpenSEESAutoComplete
items.description: An auto-complete plugin to make writing OpenSees file easier on Notepad++.

items.title: VSCode Language Support
items.description: An extension that adds rich language support for OpenSees flavoured TCL language in Visual Studio Code.

items.title: Atom Language Package
items.description: An Atom text editor package that provides syntax highlighting and auto-completion for OpenSees tcl scripts.

items.title: Editor Plugin

items.description: Simple scripts that help visualise OpenSees models or results.

items.title: Python package
items.description: A visualization framework for creating high quality and responsive renderings using glTF technology with support for both Python and Tcl.

items.title: OpenSees Model View
items.description: A Python package that can be used to visualise your OpenSees model as the tcl file is written.

items.title: OpenSees 3D Visualisation
items.description: A Python script that reads OpenSees simulation input and output files to create a 3D visualisation of your displaced model.

items.title: OpenSees Model Plotter Matlab
items.description: A Matlab-based plotter for models developed in OpenSees.

items.title: Visualiser

items.description: Application Programming Interfaces that call OpenSees.

items.title: OpenSeesAPI
items.description: A Python package that is used to write OpenSees tcl scripts quickly.

items.title: Node-OpenSees
items.description: A Node.js bind for OpenSees. (Not maintained, just for inspiration)

items.title: Script Generation via Templates
items.description: An inspiring example of using Python template engine Jinjia2 to generate massive tcl scripts.

items.title: API

items.description: If you are interested in contributing, please read the contribution guidelines. You can either contribute to the list, or contribute to the tcl codes. Your efforts are highly appreciated by the authors.
